summary: The main article describes a dual nickel- and iridium-photocatalyzed radical cascade bicyclization of 1,5-enynes to synthesize fluorenes and azepinones. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope schemes for different scaffolds, and a mechanistic proposal supported by control experiments.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Representative bioactive scaffolds.
items.description: Displays examples of biologically active molecules containing fluorene and azepine cores, such as Alsterpaullone.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Different Reactivity Patterns for Radical Cascades of Enynes
items.description: Compares previous literature methods for enyne cyclization with the current work's photoredox approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of Reaction Conditions for Radical Cyclization a
items.description: Lists the screening of catalysts, oxidants, and bases to optimize the yield and diastereoselectivity of the bicyclization reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Substrate Scope for Radical Bicyclization a -c
items.description: Shows the variety of fluorene derivatives synthesized using different 1,5-enyne substrates and radical precursors like dioxane and THF.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Substrate Scope for Azepine Derivatives a -c
items.description: Illustrates the synthesis of indeno-fused azepine scaffolds from amino-tethered enynes.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Synthetic Applications and Control Studies
items.description: Details gram-scale reactions, product transformations, and radical trapping experiments with TEMPO/BHT.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Plausible Mechanism of Intermolecular Radical Bicyclization of 1,5-Enynes
items.description: Proposes a catalytic cycle involving Ni(0)/Ni(II)/Ni(III) species and Ir(III)/Ir(IV) photoredox steps.
